title: Dedicated capacity SLA sizing, routing heuristics, and onboarding rubric
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Create a pragmatic, repeatable rubric and decision flow for incoming enterprise dedicated-capacity requests. The goal is to (1) determine SLA targets and reserved throughput sizing, (2) map workload constraints to an appropriate GPU class and scaling policy, and (3) produce an onboarding checklist and recommended contract terms. This ticket captures the proposed scoring rules, default mappings, example intake form fields, and implementation tasks for Console and Sales handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: A clear triage rubric exists with weighted scoring for SLA, throughput, model size, and regulatory needs
Default GPU-class mappings and baseline reserved throughput suggestions are documented for 3 workload archetypes
Onboarding checklist with required telemetry and prewarming steps created and linked to Console templates
Sales + Solutions have a one-page intake form and decision matrix to set customer expectations
Implementation tasks for automation in Console (pre-fill recommendations) are scoped and estimated
triage_rubric: Score components (0-10 each): SLA criticality, Traffic shape (steady vs spiky), Model complexity (params/latency profile), Data residency/compliance, Contract value/strategic importance
Weighting: SLA criticality x3, Traffic shape x2, Model complexity x2, Compliance x1.5, Contract value x1
Priority bands: 75-100 -> P0 enterprise onboarding with dedicated SLA; 50-74 -> P1 recommended reserved pool with review; <50 -> P2 self-serve or shared-hosted guidance

Example: Customer A (financial ticks, P99 500ms, spiky bursts) => SLA score 9*3 + traffic 8*2 + model 6*2 + compliance 7*1.5 = 27 + 16 + 12 + 10.5 = 65.5 -> P1 but requires burst policy and prewarming
default_sla_and_gpu_mappings: Small interactive (search/autocomplete, tokens per request <128): target P99 latency <150ms on NVidia L4 or A10G; baseline reserved throughput 100 qps; autoscale policy: horizontal scaling with burst up to 2x for 10 minutes

Medium chat (multi-turn assistants, tokens per request 128-1024): target P99 latency <400ms on A10G/A100 depending on quantization; baseline reserved throughput 20-200 concurrent sessions; autoscale policy: warm pool + fast scale-up to 3x with KV cache preservation

Large generation/embedding heavy (model >30B, long context >2048): target P99 latency <800ms on A100/H100; baseline reserved throughput specified as 'tokens/sec' based on benchmarked model profile; autoscale policy: reserved steady capacity with scheduled burst windows and contract-backed preemption rules
Fallbacks: if preferred GPU unavailable, auto-route to quantized variant on next compatible class with explicit note to customer about degraded latency/quality and cost savings option
recommended_scaling_policies: Steady workloads: allocate reserved pool sized for 95th percentile sustained throughput with 1.2x buffer; enable predictable billing and SLA
Spiky workloads: reserved baseline for 50th percentile + burst credits for short bursts (minutes); require prewarming for scheduled spikes and a burst-credit contract
Critical low-latency: pin to single-GPU execution and reserve capacity to avoid multi-tenant interference; disable noisy-neighbor autoscaling during business hours
Cost-sensitive: recommend quantized model variants with aggressive batching and KV cache; enable scheduled cold-hours scale-down
intake_form_fields: Workload archetype: interactive | chat | batch | embeddings
Traffic profile: qps, average tokens/request, 95th/99th percentile burst duration
SLA targets: P50/P95/P99 latency goals and availability SLO
Compliance requirements: data residency, PCI/PHI/controlled unclassified info
Model: name, size, repo link, quantized variants availability
Preferred GPU families and must-not-run locations
Integration constraints: VPC, on-prem connectors, private image requirements
decision_matrix_examples: Case 1 - Retail checkout assistant: moderate qps, latency P95 <250ms, not regulated -> Recommend Medium chat profile, A10G baseline, burst credits for peak hours
Case 2 - Healthcare triage model: P99 <400ms, PHI data -> Recommend Private deployment, H100/A100 reserved, strict RBAC and audit logs, contract-backed capacity
Case 3 - NLP batch embeddings for analytics: high tokens/sec but relaxed latency -> Recommend dedicated A100 pods with batch windows and aggressive quantization
